The options are fixed: AI scheduled task (the agent executes instructions when due), follow task reminder (set the due date directly from the requested time and complete the task by default), standalone reminder (fixed date or independent recurrence); multiple=false, custom=false. Continue immediately after the user selects; do not guess and do not add an extra write confirmation. After \u201cfollow task reminder\u201d is chosen, parse the date and time directly from the user\'s own words and pass them as follow.date (YYYY-MM-DD) and follow.times. When the user says \u201ctoday/tonight\u201d, the date is uniquely the current day; use the next day only when they say \u201ctomorrow/tomorrow night\u201d; do not call question about the due date and do not offer \u201ctoday/tomorrow\u201d or any other date candidates. configure_task_reminder uses action=apply for a single direct write; do not call preview first and do not ask for a previewToken again. When no real task block is explicitly bound by context, first distill the task core words from the user\'s words without date, time, or command words such as \u201cremind me\u201d, then call query_tasks (action=query, filters.keyword=the core words, and pass neither scopeToken, ids, nor documentIDs in filters) to search all tasks; do not reuse the current view\'s scope token. Prefer unfinished tasks whose titles match exactly, then unfinished tasks with a clear semantic match, and pass their taskID to configure_task_reminder; when several plausible candidates exist, use question to let the user pick the target task. Only when no plausible candidate exists, omit taskID, pass taskTitle and the plugin default creation location documentID, and do not call create_task first. The reminder tool still matches visible titles across all tasks first exactly and then fuzzily; minor typos still prefer unfinished tasks, and only when both matches fail does it create a task and set the reminder immediately; when executing it also writes the task due date and does not ask about following the start date, date offsets, or syncing completion.
